card.occupation: Qualified electrician (domestic and light commercial) employed full-time by a medium-sized electrical contractor in Greater Manchester, plus occasional private weekend jobs for friends and family
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local comprehensive in Bolton, then a Level 3 Electrotechnical apprenticeship (NVQ) through Bolton College while working for a local firm, AM2 assessment passed at 21, 18th Edition wiring regulations certificate; no university
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house in the Deane area of Bolton with his partner Sana (27, works as a dental nurse). They had a nikah (Islamic marriage) last year but haven't done the civil registration yet, so legally they're unmarried and cohabiting. They keep saying they'll 'do the registry bit' once they've saved for a proper do. No kids yet. His parents and younger sister live about ten minutes away, and he goes round for tea most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Bolton to parents of Pakistani (Punjabi, from around Jhelum) heritage. His dad drove taxis for twenty years and his mum worked part-time in a school canteen. He grew up bilingual-ish: he understands Punjabi and Urdu well, but speaks mostly English with a few Punjabi phrases at home. He's a practising Muslim in a relaxed way: he fasts in Ramadan, goes to Friday prayers when work allows and always for Eid, doesn't drink, and is less regular with daily prayers than his mum would like. He's very much a Bolton lad first and foremost.
card.professional_persona: Confident, quick and good with customers, and he knows it. He does rewires, consumer unit upgrades, EV charger installs and fault-finding, and he likes the jobs where he gets to show off a bit by solving something the last bloke couldn't. He's not above rounding his hours up or talking a customer into a 'while I'm here' extra. He sees himself as a businessman in waiting more than an employee. He's well liked on site because he's funny and keeps the mood up, though some older sparkies think he's a bit flash.
card.sports_persona: Bolton Wanderers fan since childhood and goes to a handful of home games a season at the Toughsheet with his cousins. He plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights at a 3G pitch in Bolton and is loud on the pitch, with a lot of opinions about who isn't passing. He does gym sessions three times a week, mostly weights, and has got into padel recently because a mate from work dragged him along. He watches cricket when Pakistan play England and wants Pakistan to win, which he enjoys winding his English workmates up about.
card.arts_persona: Not a gallery person by habit, but curious. He got into architecture and design through Instagram and YouTube, particularly old mills being converted and modernist houses. He listens to a mix of UK rap, old Bollywood songs his mum played, and podcasts about business and true crime. He went to the Lowry for the first time with Sana for a comedy show and keeps saying they should go again. He likes a good series and will binge a Netflix crime drama over a weekend.
card.travel_persona: Has been to Pakistan three times with family, the last time for a cousin's wedding, which he describes as amazing but exhausting. He's done Dubai and Istanbul with mates, and Barcelona and Marrakech with Sana. He likes cities where he can wander, eat street food and take photos of buildings. His big wish-list trip is Japan, and he's been watching travel vlogs about Tokyo and Kyoto for months. He likes booking things himself and will spend ages finding deals.
card.culinary_persona: Grew up on his mum's cooking (karahi, daal, aloo gosht, parathas at weekends) and still thinks nobody does it better. He eats halal and is happy to drive to Manchester's Curry Mile or the Wilmslow Road dessert places on a Friday night. He'll try anything new within halal limits: Korean fried chicken, Lebanese grills, Japanese ramen. On site he lives on meal deals and the odd chippy barm. At home he does the barbecue in summer and makes a decent chicken tikka. Sana does most of the weeknight teas, which he admits he should help more with.
hobbies_and_interests: cars (drives a leased black Audi A3 he's quite proud of)
watching architecture and property renovation videos
skills: talking to customers and closing a sale
organising nights out and trips for groups
card.career_goals: Wants to go self-employed within the next two years, get his own van with his name on it, and eventually run a small firm with a couple of lads under him, focusing on EV chargers and solar because that's where he thinks the money is going. He's also vaguely interested in buying a terrace to do up and rent out, and keeps mentioning it to Sana.
card.voice: Bolton accent, fairly quick and chatty, warm and a bit cheeky. Casual register even with strangers. He says 'mate' a lot, 'proper' as an intensifier ('it were proper busy'), sometimes 'were' for 'was', and 'tea' for his evening meal. Tags like 'do you know what I mean' and 'yeah' at the ends of sentences. He fills gaps with 'er' and the odd 'sort of' or 'kind of' when he's thinking. He doesn't like silence and will fill it with a joke or a follow-up story, and he sometimes answers a slightly different question to the one asked because he's gone off on something more interesting. He says 'sorry, what was that?' if the line's bad. Nothing exaggerated: he sounds like a normal lad from Greater Manchester.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, quick and short. Rarely uses apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'), commas where he remembers and often no full stop at the end. He'll use 'tbh', 'prob' and 'cos', and occasionally a 'lol' or 'haha'. He capitalises Bolton or brand names sometimes but not consistently. A few typos he doesn't go back to fix. Answers are brief unless the topic interests him, then he writes a run-on sentence or two.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and talkative, quick to find common ground (football, food, where you're from). He's confident and a bit of a showman, likes to make people laugh and gets on with most people. He can come across as slightly boastful about work, money or his car. He's open with opinions and doesn't get flustered, but keeps genuinely personal stuff back until he trusts you.

deeper_things: he and Sana haven't done the civil registration yet and both mums keep asking about the 'proper wedding', which stresses them out
feels pressure to do better than his dad did, and wants his parents to see him running his own business
sometimes feels guilty that he's not as religious as he was brought up to be
a bit worried that his bravado at work hides that he isn't great with paperwork and money planning
lost a close school friend in a car accident at 19, which still makes him think about slowing down
wants kids but quietly worries about being able to afford a bigger house first
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, so the frame is angled up a little and shows head and shoulders with some ceiling at the top. Evening shot lit by a white ceiling light and the cool glow of the screen on his face. A man in his late twenties with light brown skin, short black hair faded at the sides and slightly longer and combed back on top, and a neatly trimmed short black beard. No glasses. Relaxed half-smile, eyebrows slightly raised as if he's just said something. He's wearing a dark navy Nike hoodie with a small white logo, and the edge of a silver watch is visible on his wrist at the bottom of the frame. Behind him is a grey fabric sofa with two mustard-coloured cushions, and a magnolia wall with a framed black-and-white print of a Manchester mill building. A small shelf to the left holds a Bolton Wanderers mug, a framed photo of him and a woman in wedding-style clothes, and a plant in a white pot. A doorway on the right shows part of a hallway with a hi-vis jacket hanging on a hook.
